note.title: Possessives
note.overview: Distinguish own from someone else's and select the correct school-table form.
learningGoals: Distinguish own from someone else's possession.
Recall the forms printed in the possessive table.
mustMemoriseRules: suus points back to the subject and agrees with the possessed noun.
eius eorum and earum identify a different owner and do not agree with the possessed noun.

commonMistakes: Using suus for someone else's possession.
Making eius agree with the possessed noun.
A familiar stem with the wrong case, number, person or tense ending is not correct.
detailedExplanation: Distinguish own from someone else's and select the correct school-table form.
Agreement depends on case, number and gender. Find the noun or role that controls the form, then choose the matching ending; do not select a form only because it looks familiar.
examTips: Mark the finite verb first, then use noun endings to assign subject, object and recipient roles.
Normal Latin word order can vary; the case, number, gender, person and tense endings cannot.
For English to Latin, build each required form before arranging the sentence.
